chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when he married Maymuna bint al-Harith, gave a banquet (Waleema) for it and fed the people Al-Hays (a mixture of dates and butter).

key_terms.أَوْلَمَ: He gave a banquet or wedding feast (Waleema)
key_terms.الْحَيْسَ: Al-Hays, a traditional dish made of dates and butter/ghee
key_terms.مَيْمُونََةَ: Maymuna, a wife of the Prophet (SAWW)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) do to celebrate his marriage to Maymuna bint al-Harith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the Sunnah of the Waleema (marriage banquet) by citing the Prophet’s (SAW) specific practice of hosting Maymuna bint al-Harith and serving 'Al-Hays'—a traditional mixture of dates, cheese, and flour—to the community. It underscores the Shia emphasis on communal generosity and the Prophet’s role in setting practical, accessible norms for marital celebrations, reinforcing the social dimension of marriage in Islamic jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said when he<sup>saww</sup> married Maymouna daughter of Al-Haris, gave a banquet (Waleema) over it and fed Al-Hays (dates with butter) to the people’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Um ay r from Hisham ibn Salim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

when the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, married Maymunah, daughter of al-Harith, he served food to people and it was mashed dates with the stones removed, with ghee.’”
